**Choice selects a category; Noul estimates whether a statement is true.** Both are typed Jev question types. [Official documentation](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives)

| | Choice | Noul |
|---|---|---|
| Question | “Which of these options?” | “Is this true?” |
| Input | Instructions plus a `criteria` map of named options | Instructions; optional criteria clarifying yes/no |
| Output | Selected `choice`, per-option `probabilities`, and `confidence` | A single `noul` probability from 0 to 1; no separate confidence |
| Example | Route a ticket to billing, support, or sales | Determine whether the customer requests a refund |

For Noul, `0.9` means a 90% estimated probability of **yes**; `0.1` strongly favors **no**; `0.5` means equal probability—not “half true.” Your code chooses the threshold for acting. Use Choice when you need a named category and Noul when you need a yes/no probability. [TypeSafe’s selection guidance](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives#choose-a-question-type)
